text.p01: To everyone who has ever said, "I can do it myself." The circle is wider than you think. A story about asking for help and letting others give.
text.p03: High in the mountains, where clouds come to rest, lived Killa, a little chinchilla with silver fur and the fastest feet on the slope.
text.p04: On Killa's mountain, everybody helped everybody. When one family needed something, the others came running. Paw to paw, round and round!
text.p05: And Killa always came first. She carried seeds for the viscachas and soft grass for the guinea pigs, all in her little striped bag.
text.p06: But when anyone tried to help Killa back, she just laughed and shook her head. "No, thank you! I can do it myself!"
text.p07: Her best friend Sami, a young vicuña, offered to carry her heavy bag. "No, thank you," said Killa. "I'm fine!"
text.p08: Sami's ears drooped a little, but Killa didn't notice. She was already racing off to help tiny Kinti the hummingbird.
text.p09: Then one evening, while Killa was out helping the guinea pigs, a hailstorm came rattling over the mountain. When it stopped, she hurried home.
text.p10: Her wall had tumbled, and her burrow was full of hail. Her friends came running, but Killa shook her head. "I can do it myself."
text.p11: All night Killa pushed and pulled, but the stones were too heavy. At sunrise, Sami sat beside her. "Helping is like playing catch," he said.
text.p12: "You throw and throw, but you never let anyone throw back." Asking felt harder than lifting any stone. But Killa asked, "Will you help me?"
text.p13: "Yes!" everyone cheered. The viscachas rolled stones. The guinea pigs carried grass. Sami lifted the biggest rocks. Paw to paw, round and round!
text.p14: Being helped felt strange at first, like wearing somebody else's warm sweater. Then it didn't feel strange at all. It just felt warm.
text.p15: By evening, Killa's burrow was cozier than ever, with a strong new wall and a soft grass bed from the guinea pigs.
text.p16: "Thank you," said Killa. "Thank YOU," the viscachas beamed, "for letting us!" Killa blinked. Letting them help had made them happy too!
text.p17: Deep in the cold season came the biggest snow of all. By morning, burrows all over the mountain were buried, with little noses peeking out.
text.p18: This time, Killa didn't try to dig alone. She ran from burrow to burrow, asking, "Who needs help? And who can help?"
text.p19: But Kinti the hummingbird stayed on her branch, all fluffed up. "I can't help anybody," she peeped. "I'm too small. So I can't ask."
text.p20: "Everyone has something to give," said Killa. "You can fly up high and see what we can't!" Kinti zoomed up. "Over there! And there!"
text.p21: All day they went around the mountain, burrow by burrow, everyone digging for everyone, with Kinti calling the way. Paw to paw, round and round!
text.p22: At sunset, every burrow was open, even Kinti's snowy rock nook. Everyone had given, and everyone had received. Killa felt warm down to her toes.
text.p23: From then on, Killa still helped everyone. But when friends offered help, she said, "Yes, please!" And when she needed something, she asked.
text.p24: Paw to paw, round and round, the help kept flowing all over the mountain. Help is a circle. Let it come back around. The End
text.cover: The Circle of Paws. A Story About Asking for Help and Letting Others Give
